title: Count Number of Homogenous Substrings
description:
Count Number of Homogenous Substrings

Given a string s, return the number of homogenous substrings of s. Since the answer may be too large, return it modulo 109 + 7.

A string is homogenous if all the characters of the string are the same.

A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters within a string.

Examples:

  • Input: s = "abbcccaa"
    Output: 13
    Explanation: The homogenous substrings are listed as below:
    "a" appears 3 times.
    "aa" appears 1 time.
    "b" appears 2 times.
    "bb" appears 1 time.
    "c" appears 3 times.
    "cc" appears 2 times.
    "ccc" appears 1 time.
    3 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 13.
  • Input: s = "xy"
    Output: 2
    Explanation: The homogenous substrings are "x" and "y".
  • Input: s = "zzzzz"
    Output: 15

Constraints:

  • 1 <= s.length <= 105
  • s consists of lowercase letters.
solution_text:
Track the Current Run

Suppose the equal-character run ending at the current position has length r. There are exactly r new homogenous substrings ending here: the last character, the last two characters, and so on through the whole run.

Reset the run length to 1 when the character changes; otherwise increase it. Adding the current run length at every position counts every valid substring once.

Time: O(n). Space: O(1).
solution_code:
def countHomogenous(s):
    MOD = 1000000007
    answer = 0
    run_length = 0
    previous = ''
    for character in s:
        if character == previous:
            run_length += 1
        else:
            previous = character
            run_length = 1

        # Every suffix of the current equal-character run is a new
        # homogenous substring ending at this position.
        answer = (answer + run_length) % MOD
    return answer
